Name: Glasgow-4006
bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]] {{Estimated Date|Birth}} == Biography == '''Robert Glasgow''' was the son of [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow of uncertain Corsoun]] and Andrew's wife '''Elizat Stevinsoun'''. Andrew's testament, made on 6 February 1597/8, expressly describes him as:
“Robart Glasgw his sone begottin be him vpoun the said Elizat his wyff”
Andrew directed that Elizat should “bruik his [word unclear] land quhill his said Robart cum to aige,” showing that Robert had not yet attained the relevant legal majority and was intended to succeed to the land after Elizat's interim possession.National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8, death stated as 7 February, confirmed 10 July 1598; corrected working transcription of the original register images. Printed index: Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108]. The testament also names Andrew's daughters Marion, Janet and Isobel. It makes conditional provision “incais his said spous be with bairne to him”; that does not prove that an additional child was born. == Research Notes == === Identity === The profile previously represented an Andrew Glasgow created from a superseded reading of this testament; the corrected record names no such son. It has been repurposed for the directly documented son Robert. [[Glasgow-1156]], estimated born in 1582 and buried at Duddingston in 1647, is compatible by date and Lothian geography but its record names neither Andrew, Elizat, Corsoun, siblings nor the land, so it is excluded as the present match. [[Glasgow-1027]] is the proved son of Ninian Glasgow and Jonet Meik, and [[Glasgow-1096]] died before Andrew's will. Search NRS GD150/696–757, GD150/2027–2060 and GD150/320–493 for Andrew's land and an occupier succession to Robert. == Sources ==

Name: Glasgow-4095
bio:
[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
{{Estimated Date|Birth}}

== Biography ==

'''Marion Glasgow''' was a daughter of [[Glasgow-3163|Andrew Glasgow of uncertain Corsoun]]. Andrew's testament, made on 6 February 1597/8, provides that if his wife Elizat Stevinsoun was not pregnant, his third was to be divided among “his said sone and his said [dochter… struck through] Marione, Jonet, Isobell.”<ref name="Andrew1598">National Records of Scotland, Edinburgh Commissary Court, CC8/8/32, images 123–124, testament testamentar and inventory of Andro Glasgw, made 6 February 1597/8, death stated as 7 February, confirmed 10 July 1598; corrected working transcription of the original register images. Printed index: Scottish Record Society, ''Commissariot of Edinburgh: Register of Testaments, 1514–1600'', [https://archive.org/details/scottishrecordso01scotuoft/page/n117/mode/1up p. 108].</ref>

Her brother [[Glasgow-4006|Robert]] is expressly called Andrew's son by Elizat. The testament does not separately state that Elizat was this daughter's mother, so maternity should not be inferred as certain from this clause alone.<ref name="Andrew1598"/>

== Research Notes ==

=== Identity ===

Named as a lawful daughter in Andrew's 1598 testament. No later record has been securely connected to her; the same-name Glasgow women of the period have no Corsoun, Stevenson, sibling or succession bridge to this household, so none is attached here.

A separate [[Glasgow-3062|Marion Glasgow]] is identified as [[Glasgow-3188|Ninian Glasgow]]'s sister in his 1613 testament and as the mother of James Fultoun in a 1610 Glasgow baptism. Neither record names Andrew, Elizat or Corsoun. This is a same-name identity comparison, not a proved match; keep the profiles separate pending a connecting record.<ref>National Records of Scotland, Glasgow Commissary Court, CC9/7/9, images 142–145, Ninian Glasgow testament; Glasgow & West of Scotland Family History Society, [https://www.gwsfhs.org.uk/records/james-fultoun/ James Fultoun baptism index], 7 August 1610.</ref>
